comparison: Both evaluations agree that the structural determination of Nup188N is well-supported. OpenEval focuses on crystallographic details (C3, C4, C40, C42-C53), while peer review encompasses a broader set including SH3-like domain and Nup188C structures. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse publication and call the structure 'a very important step' for the field.

Both agree the SH3-like domain characterization (C54-C61) is well-supported by crystal structure and sequence data. Peer review includes these claims in their comprehensive endorsement of the structural work without specific challenges.

Both agree the Nup188C structure and flexibility observations (C5, C62-C65) are supported by crystallographic data. Peer review encompasses these claims in their overall positive assessment of the structural determination.

Both agree the computational modeling and EM validation of conformational heterogeneity (C66-C72) are well-supported. Peer review includes these structural characterization claims in their comprehensive endorsement without challenge.

Both agree the structural comparison between Nup188 and Nup192 (C73-C83) is supported by sequence analysis and EM data. Peer review includes these claims in their overall positive assessment of the structural work.

Perfect overlap on claims C6, C84-C90. Both agree the structural similarity data between Nup188/192 and NTRs is well-supported with appropriate RMSD values. Peer reviewers acknowledge the relationship without challenging the structural comparison results.

Both address FG-binding claims (C7, C91, C92). OpenEval finds the pulldown data well-supported with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers do not challenge the data itself but question the novelty and interpretation, noting that similar interactions were previously reported for Nic96p (Schrader 2008).

High overlap on negative Ran-binding data (C94-C96). Both agree this negative result is appropriately documented with proper controls and distinguishes Nup188/192 from canonical NTRs. Neither evaluation challenges this finding.

High overlap on nuclear translocation claims (C8, C97-C104). OpenEval finds the data well-supported with appropriate controls and statistical analysis. Peer reviewers challenge the interpretation, noting that WGA inhibition only proves transport through pores (not necessarily facilitated passage) and suggesting alternative mechanisms for importin-β competition beyond direct competition for FG-repeats.

Both address additional translocation characterization (C105-C106). OpenEval finds the Ran pre-wash and dilution experiments support energy-independent translocation. Peer reviewers' concerns about the overall translocation interpretation (R4) extend to these supporting experiments.

Both address evolutionary relationship claims (C9, C10, C122). OpenEval notes these are explicitly speculative and require additional phylogenetic analysis. Peer reviewers challenge the framing, stating the title is misleading because while Nup188/192 share FG-binding with NTRs, they don't share transport function. Both agree the claims need more careful qualification.

Partial overlap on functional speculation about flexibility (C111-C112). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN because functional implications are explicitly speculative without direct experimental evidence. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these as reasonable possibilities by not critiquing them, rating the broader speculative claims as SUPPORTED.

Perfect overlap on functional divergence claims (C113-C116). Both agree the differential phenotypes are supported by cited studies and the SH3-like domain distinction is structurally supported. Both appropriately note the mechanistic connection remains speculative but accept the overall claims.

Partial overlap on NPC biogenesis speculation (C127-C129). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN because claims are explicitly speculative without direct experimental validation. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these hypotheses as reasonable possibilities consistent with the data by not challenging them.

High overlap on FG-repeat structural role claims (C130-C134). OpenEval notes these are speculative and lack direct evidence for structural role in NPC integrity. Peer reviewers also express uncertainty, noting the claims are consistent with some previous models (Schrader 2008) but overstate novelty and don't actually challenge all current paradigms as suggested.

Partial overlap on FG-repeat organization paradigm claims (C135-C136). OpenEval notes these are explicitly speculative and require structural studies in intact NPCs. Peer reviewers agree the claims overstate novelty, noting they only question specific models (Rout/Lim entropic repulsion) but are consistent with mesh-based barrier models.

Partial overlap on evolutionary scenario speculation (C119, C120, C123, C124). OpenEval notes these appropriately acknowledge limitations and present alternative scenarios as speculation requiring phylogenetic analysis. Peer reviewers' concerns about the evolutionary/functional relationship framing align with OpenEval's assessment that these claims need more careful qualification.
